title: Nine Minutes Before Dawn
subtitle: 战争与和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：attack　|　正文 317 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 attack 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1944 my grandfather was in ① an attack that began at four in the morning and was over by nine, and he said the waiting had been worse. The ② attack, meaning the thing that happened and not the order that caused it, took nine minutes and a field; an attack, he said, is the only plan that survives being carried out. He said most plans do not.

Every ③ attack he ever described began with noise and ended with counting, and he said the counting was the part he never got used to. Their ④ attack had been planned for nine days and changed on the night; an attack, my father said, is the only thing that is decided twice, once by the planners and once by the men. He said the second decision is the one that counts.

My grandmother used the word differently and meant ⑤ an attack of the chest, which she had every winter from 1958. The ⑥ attack, meaning the illness and not the battle, is the only enemy that arrives without being ordered to; an attack, she said, is the only word that covers both an army and a cough. She said the cough lasted nine weeks.

By 1969 the ⑦ attack had become a paragraph in a book that got nine things wrong. The ⑧ attack on him in the paper that March was nine lines long and unsigned; an attack, my mother said, is either a thing soldiers do or a thing writers do, and both are easier from behind. She said the unsigned part was the cowardice.

The  attack I remember is the one at four in the morning, which he described once and never again. An  attack, he said in 1971, is the only thing that everybody plans and nobody remembers as planned; every attack, he said, is nine minutes of noise and forty years of counting. He said the counting never ends.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 进攻；攻击（一次具体的军事进攻）
B. n. 进攻（指实际发生的那件事，与命令相对）
C. n. 进攻（指被写成书里一段话的那一次）
D. 固定搭配：be in an attack 参加一次进攻
F. n. 发作（抽象：疾病来袭这件事）
G. n. 抨击；批评（言论上的攻击）
H. n. 进攻（抽象总称；泛指）

items.q: an attack that began at four in the morning
The attack, meaning the thing that happened
The attack, meaning the illness and not the battle
the attack had become a paragraph
The attack on him in the paper

answers.why: be in an attack 意为“参加一次进攻”，1944 年祖父参加了一次凌晨四点开始、九点前结束的进攻，他说等待更难受。
attack 指“实际发生的那件事”，与命令相对，这次进攻用了九分钟和一片田地。
attack 为抽象总称，泛指“进攻这类事”，他描述过的每一次进攻都以喧闹开始、以清点结束。
attack 意为“一次具体的军事进攻”，他们那次进攻筹划了九天，当天夜里又改了。
attack 意为“（疾病的）发作”，祖母说的是另一回事：她从 1958 年起每年冬天都要发作的胸口毛病。
attack 意为“发作（疾病来袭这件事）”，与战斗相对，它是唯一不待命令就到的敌人。
attack 指被写成书里一段话的那一次进攻，到 1969 年那次进攻成了书里的一段话，而那本书弄错了九件事。
attack 意为“抨击、批评”，那年三月报纸上对他的那篇抨击只有九行，而且没有署名。
